scripts.//check:comment-only: NOT a gate -- an ad-hoc proof, run as: npm run check:comment-only -- --strict <before> <after> (get <before> with: git show <sha>:<path> > tmp). Several files in this tree are FROZEN for the duration of a task, and that freeze has been lifted three times, each time requiring the edit to be proven COMMENT-ONLY mechanically rather than asserted. This is that proof, kept as a script so the next person does not re-derive it WRONG. The first version (commit e3724ee3) compared a raw ts.createScanner token stream, which is UNSAFE on every spec file in this repository: a scanner has no parser above it, so a backtick inside a JSDoc comment desynchronises its template-literal pairing and it swallows whole comment blocks into a single token, reporting a comment-only edit as a code change. Measured doing exactly that on tests/38-editor-drag.spec.ts during WS-HMI-2 Task 11 fix round 1. The script uses a full parse instead, plus a second compiler-free line filter that shares no code with it, and prints sensitivity/specificity controls on EVERY run -- because 'the two files agree' means nothing until you know the instruments can tell code from comment in both directions. See the script's own header for the full reasoning.
